dimensions.label: Plan near the $130 entry price
dimensions.a: SEO: $139.95/mo, 500 keywords tracked daily, no historical data, no API access
dimensions.b: Lite: $129/mo, 750 keywords tracked weekly, 6 months of history, API included

dimensions.label: Free trial before you pay
dimensions.a: 7-day free trial on SEO, Starter and Pro+ (a card is required)
dimensions.b: No free trial on any paid plan

dimensions.label: How often rankings refresh
dimensions.b: Weekly, on every plan, including Enterprise

dimensions.label: Historical ranking and traffic data
dimensions.a: Not included on the SEO plan; not stated for Starter, Pro+ or Advanced
dimensions.b: 6 months on Lite, up to 5 years on Advanced, unlimited on Enterprise

dimensions.label: Room to add teammates
dimensions.a: No published seat cap; each extra login costs $45 to $100 a month
dimensions.b: Lite tops out at 3 users total; Standard at 6; Advanced at 11

dimensions.label: How an extra seat is billed
dimensions.a: One flat price per plan: $45, $80 or $100 a user a month
dimensions.b: Metered by usage on Lite ($20 to $40); a flat $60 to $100 a user a month from Standard up

dimensions.label: AI-search prompts bundled into the plan
dimensions.a: 50 to 200 of your own prompts tracked daily, bundled from Starter up
dimensions.b: 5 to 20 of your own prompts tracked daily, bundled from Lite up

dimensions.label: Checking any brand's AI visibility with no setup
dimensions.a: Not sold as a standalone lookup; only your own configured prompts
dimensions.b: Brand Radar's AI Visibility Index, from $199/mo, no prompts to configure

dimensions.label: Refund if you change your mind
dimensions.a: 7-day money-back guarantee on annual plans and add-on purchases
dimensions.b: No general refunds; a discretionary exception for unused monthly plans

verdicts.why: An agency managing several client sites gets more tracked keywords, API access from Lite up, and cheaper extra seats from Ahrefs than from Semrush's matching plans.
A freelancer working solo pays less on Ahrefs' Lite plan than on Semrush's SEO plan for more tracked keywords, though only Semrush lets you try before you commit with its 7-day trial.

An online store tracking many product and category keywords gets more headroom for less money from Ahrefs' Lite plan than from Semrush's SEO plan, at a similar monthly crawl allowance for technical audits.

A single-location service business needs its Google Business Profile ranking locally, not backlink research, and Semrush is the only one of the two with a standalone Local Toolkit built for exactly that, at $30 a location a month.

A coach or course creator's traffic usually comes from content, email and paid social rather than technical SEO, so neither platform's keyword-tracking plans are the first tool worth paying for at this stage.

An early-stage startup gets more from Ahrefs before spending anything, since Ahrefs Free monitors a verified domain indefinitely and Starter adds keyword tracking for $29 a month with no annual lock-in.
